Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:10:1.english: This one emerged first - And he is the firstborn.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:10:2.hebrew: אם הוחזקה על עומדה - כדמפרש, דלא אהדרא אפה — נאמנת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:10:2.english: If she has stood in her place - As [the Gemara] explains, that she did not turn her face away — she is deemed credible.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:10:3.hebrew: ואם לאו - דאהדרא אפה, אינה נאמנת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:10:3.english: And if not - [In a case] where she turned her face away, she is not deemed credible.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:11:1.english: Who were sleeping - In Tractate Niddah (61a), [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to when they were] intertwined and clinging to one another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:11:2.hebrew: כשיעור ווסת - לאחר מציאה מיד. ובמסכת נדה (דף יד:) מפרש שיעור ווסת: שעומד העד — הוא הקינוח — בצד המשקוף, ואינו מחוסר אלא לקנח מיד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:11:2.english: Within the duration of a veset - Immediately after the finding [of the blood]. And in tractate Niddah (daf 14b), it explains the duration of a veset: that the examination cloth — that is, the wiping cloth — stands alongside the doorpost, and nothing is lacking except to wipe immediately:

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:12:1.hebrew: זה כהן וזה לוי - נשים שילדו בבית, אחת אשת כהן, ולוי, נתין, וממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:12:1.english: This [one is] a priest and this [one is] a Levite - Women who gave birth in [the same] house: one [was] the wife of a priest, and [the others the wives of a] Levite, a Gibeonite, and a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:12:2.hebrew: שלא קרא עליה ערער - שלא יצא מעורר על הולד, לומר: זה בנה של אשת ממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:12:2.english: When no objection was raised against it - That an objector did not come forward concerning the child, to say: This is the son of the wife of a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:14:1.english: Where he has a presumption of validity - That they held him in the presumption of being valid.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:14:2.english: But where he has no presumption of validity - For it was not known to people who is the valid one, and not one of them has emerged from doubt.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:1.english: The seller is deemed credible - [This is] the latter clause of the baraita [quoted] above.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:2.hebrew: לזה מכרתי כו' - אם שנים מעוררין על המקח: זה אומר "מכרת לי", וזה אומר "לי מכרת, ושלי המקח". לקמן מוקי ליה ששניהם נתנו לו דמים, כל אחד ואחד דמים שלמים — אחד מדעתו ואחד בעל כרחו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:2.english: I sold to this [one], etc. - If two [people] dispute the purchase: this one says, "You sold [it] to me," and that one says, "To me you sold [it], and the purchased item is mine." Later, [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to a case] where both of them gave him money, each one full payment — one with his consent, and one against his will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:3.hebrew: בזמן שמקחו בידו - דרמיא עליה למידק, שלא לחזור לו מזה ולהחזיר לו דמיו ויתן המקח למי שלא נמכר לו, דקם ליה במי שפרע. הילכך, מידק דייק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:3.english: When the purchased item is in his possession - For it is incumbent upon him to pay close attention, so as not to renege on this one and return his money to him, and give the purchased item to the one to whom it was not sold, as he would [thereby] be subject to [the curse of] *Mi Shepara*. Therefore, he is certainly precise.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:4.hebrew: אבל בזמן שאין מקחו בידו - ושניהם אוחזין בו, אינו נאמן, דכיון דלאו עליה רמיא, תו לא דייק לזכור למי הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:15:4.english: But when the item being purchased is not in his possession - And both of them are holding it, he is not deemed credible, for since [the responsibility] does not rest upon him, he no longer pays careful attention to remember to whom it [belongs].

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:1.hebrew: אין בו משום אסופי - דאי לאו דכשר הוא, לא הוה טרחא ביה למימהל ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:1.english: He is not subject to [the status of] a foundling - For if he were not legitimate, [his mother] would not have troubled herself to circumcise him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:2.english: His limbs are adjusted - His limbs are set and straightened.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:3.hebrew: אין בו משום אסופי - דאי פסול הוא, לא הוה מתקנא ליה, הואיל ודעתה להשליכו; אלא, מחמת רעבון הושלך. ל"א: "משלטי הדמיה" — איבריו גדולים, ומלובן ומזורז. אין זה מזנה, אלא מבעלה, שמתוך תשמיש תדיר הולד מלובן ומזורז, כדאמר במסכת נדה (דף לא.): ג' חדשים אחרונים, תשמיש יפה לאשה ויפה לולד, שמתוך כך הולד מזורז ומלובן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:3.english: He is not subject to [the status of] a foundling - For if he were of unfit [lineage], she would not have tended to him [to straighten his limbs], since it was her intention to abandon him; rather, he was abandoned due to famine. Another explanation: “His limbs are adjusted” — His limbs are large, and he is fair-skinned and vigorous. This [child] is not from illicit relations, but from her husband, because through frequent intercourse the fetus becomes fair-skinned and vigorous, as it says in Tractate Niddah (31a): The final three months, intercourse is beneficial for the woman and beneficial for the fetus, for through this the child emerges vigorous and fair-skinned.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:4.hebrew: הדמיה - איבריו, כמו ״הדומי ניהדמיה״ דעירובין (דף ל.), ״והדמין תתעבדון״ דדניאל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:4.english: His limbs - Means his limbs; like “shall we cut it into limbs” in Eruvin (page 30a), and “you shall be cut into pieces” in Daniel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:5.english: Filled with kohl - Around his eyes, to beautify him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:6.hebrew: רמי חומרי - קשרים שעושים לרפואה ותולין לתינוק, דאמרינן במסכת שבת (דף סו:): הבנים יוצאים בקשרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:6.english: Knots were placed [upon him] - Knots that are made for healing and hung on an infant, as we say in Tractate Shabbat (daf 66b): “Boys may go out with knots.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:7.english: A note was hanging - A written amulet.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:8.english: An amulet was hanging [on him] - [An amulet] of roots.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:9.hebrew: אין בו משום אסופי - דהא חסה על חייו, והוכיח תחילתה שאוהבתו, ולא השליכתו למות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:1:9.english: He is not subject to [the status of] a foundling - For [his mother] took pity on his life, and her initial actions proved that she loves him and did not cast him out to die.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:2:1.hebrew: תלי בדיקלא אי מטיא ליה חיה רעה - ויכולה לטורפו משם, יש בו משום אסופי. כללו של דבר: כל מקום שיש להבין דלדעת מיתה השליכתהו ולא חסה עליו, יש בו משום אסופי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:2:1.english: Hanging from a palm tree, if a wild beast can reach him - and is able to prey upon him from there, he is subject to [the status of] a foundling. The general rule of the matter: Any place where it is to be understood that she cast him out intending [his] death and had no pity on him, he is subject to [the status of] a foundling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:3:1.hebrew: זרדתא דסמיכא למתא - אי תלי באילן ששמו זרדתא, שלרי"ר (שורביי"ר: חוזרר (אילן)) בלע"ז — אי סמיכא למתא, אע"ג דלא מטיא ליה חיה, יש בו משום אסופי; דאמר בערבי פסחים (פסחים דף קיא:): זרדתא דסמיכא למתא לא פחיתא משתין שידי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:3:1.english: A sorb-tree that is near a town - If [the child] was hanging from a tree whose name is zardeta — chelrier (sorbier: sorb [tree]) in the vernacular — if it is near a town, even though a wild animal cannot reach him, he is subject to [the status of] a foundling; for [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 111b): A sorb-tree that is near a town has no fewer than sixty demons.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:3:2.hebrew: בי כנישתא - בתי כנסיות שלהם חוץ לעיר הוו, ואי לא שכיחי בה רבים, כגון אורחים, יש לדאג ממזיקים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:3:2.english: A synagogue - Their synagogues were outside the city, and if people are not frequently found there, such as guests, there is [cause] to worry about harmful spirits.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:4:1.hebrew: פירא דסופלי - נמצא בחפירה העשויה להטיל שם גרעיני תמרים למאכל בהמות — יש בו משום אסופי, דחוץ לעיר עבדי ליה, ושכיחי בהו מזיקין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:4:1.english: A pit of date pits - [If he was] found in a pit made for casting date pits there for animal fodder, he is subject to [the status of] a foundling, for they make it outside the city, and harmful spirits are common in them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:4:2.hebrew: חריפתא דנהרא - נתנוהו בעריבה והשליכתהו לאמצעית הנהר, מקום שהספינות עוברות תמיד — אין בו משום אסופי, דלכך טרחה להוליכו עד חריפות הנהר, שיעברו ספינות שם וימצאוהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:4:2.english: The swift current of the river - [If] they placed him in a trough and she cast him into the middle of the river, a place where boats pass constantly — he does not have the status of a foundling; for she took the trouble to carry him to the swift current of the river for this [reason]: so that boats would pass there and find him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:4:3.hebrew: פישרא - מקום שיפוע הנהר ע"י הפשרת שלגים, שאין דרך ספינות לעבור שם — יש בו משום אסופי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:4:3.english: Meltwater [pishra] - The place of the river's slope [flooded] through the melting of snow, where boats are not accustomed to pass — [a child found there] is subject to [the status of] a foundling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:6:1.english: Are deemed credible with regard to him - To say, "He is our son."

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:7:1.hebrew: בשני רעבון - שהרבה נשלכין, לא רצו חכמים לפוסלם מחמת יציאת קול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:7:1.english: In years of famine - Since many [children] are abandoned, the Sages did not want to disqualify them on account of a rumor having spread.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:8:1.hebrew: נאמנים לאלתר - ולא לאחר זמן, אבל כל שאר הנאמנין נאמנים נמי לאחר זמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:8:1.english: Are deemed credible immediately - And not after a lapse of time; but all other credible [people] are also deemed credible after a lapse of time.

Rashi on Kiddushin 73b:8:2.english: And one who exempts her companions - From [ritual] impurity, as [the Gemara] explains.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 73b:15:1.hebrew: בד"א בזמן שמקחו בידו - פירש בקונטרס: דרמי עליה למידק, לפי שהוא ב"מי שפרע" אם יחזור במי שנתן המעות ויחזיר לו דמיו; אבל בזמן שאין מקחו בידו, אלא שניהם אוחזים בו — אינו נאמן, דכיון דלא עליה רמיא, לא דייק לזכור מי הוה. ופריך: "וניחזי זוזי ממאן נקיט?" — א"אין מקחו בידו" פריך לפירוש הקונטרס, דפי' שלא קבל המעות אלא מאחד מהם, והא ודאי מידכר דכיר ממאן קביל זוזי; ומשני: "אלא דנקיט זוזי מתרוייהו ולא ידיע כו'". ולפי זה אמרינן: דאפילו אמר שידע — לא להימני, משום דלא רמי עליה למידק. כך שיטת הקונטרס. ומה שפי' דפריך א"אין מקחו בידו", דקאמר דאינו נאמן, ופריך: "וניחזי זוזי ממאן נקט?", פירוש: ולאותו שנתן לו המעות ודאי נתרצה — קשה: דמאי יש לנו להאמינו טפי מעד אחד דעלמא? דכיון שאין מקחו בידו, לא שייך לומר מיגו כדי להאמינו! לכן פי' ר"ת: "בזמן שמקחו בידו", ואז הוא נאמן מטעם מיגו, דמצי אמר: "לא מכרתי" או "חזרתי וקניתיו"; אבל "אין מקחו בידו" — אינו נאמן, דאז לא שייך מיגו. ופריך: "וליחזי זוזי ממאן נקט" — נהי נמי דמקחו בידו, אמאי נאמן אם יאמר אמי שלא קבל המעות: "לזה נתרציתי"? דמשמע דנאמן בכל ענין. ואמאי נאמן? הוה מיגו במקום עדים, דאנן סהדי דלאותו שנתן המעות נתרצה! ומשני: "דנקיט זוזי כו'". ולפי זה גרסי': "ולא ידיע", ולא גר': "ולא ידע", דמשמע שאין אנו חוששין לידיעתו — דודאי חיישינן לידיעתו אי הוה ידע! ולפי זה צ"ל: שלא ידע, שאם ידע — הוה אמרי': נתרצה לזה. אך בריש בבא מציעא (דף ב:), גבי שנים אוחזים בטלית דמוקי לה בגמרא במקח וממכר, ופריך: "מקח וממכר — ניחזי זוזי ממאן נקט?", ופירש התם רש"י כפי שיטתו דהכא. ועוד פירש התם: אע"ג דאמר בפ' בתרא דקידושין דבזמן שאין מקחו בידו אינו נאמן, והכא הוי כאין מקחו בידו, דתרוייהו אדוקין בטלית, ואמאי פריך שיהא המוכר נאמן? הא מוקמינן התם בדנקט זוזי מתרוייהו, והשתא ס"ד דלא נקט זוזי אלא מחד. אך לפר"ת קשה: דמאי פריך התם: "וניחזי זוזי ממאן נקיט?" והא לפירושו, אע"ג דלא נקיט זוזי אלא מחד, אין לנו להאמינו, כדפרישית! לכך צ"ל התם: "וניחזי זוזי ממאן נקט" — כלומר, היכי קתני במתני': "זה ישבע שאין לו בה פחות מחציה כו'", נשאל למוכר ממאן קבל המעות, וליהוי כעד אחד לפטור את מי שמסייע אפי' משבועת היסת, ולחייב את שכנגדו שבועה דאורייתא! אבל להוציא ממון מזה ולמסור לזה — פשיטא דאינו נאמן, רק כדפרישית. ומשני: "דנקיט זוזי מתרוייהו". וגם לפירוש זה גרסי': "לא ידע", אך אם הוא ידע — פשיטא שאנו חוששין לידיעתו לחייב לזה שבועה דאורייתא, כדפירשתי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 73b:15:1.english: In what case is this statement said? When the item being purchased is in his possession - Rashi explained that it is incumbent upon him to be precise, because he would be subject to the curse of "He Who took retribution" (Mi ShePara) if he retracts against the one who gave the money and returns his money to him. But when the item being purchased is not in his possession, but rather both of them are holding it, he is not deemed credible, because since it is not incumbent upon him [to return the money], he does not pay close attention to remember who it was. And [the Gemara] asks: "And let us see from whom he took the money?" — It asks this on [the clause] "if the item being purchased is not in his possession" according to Rashi's explanation, as he explained that he only accepted the money from one of them; and he certainly remembers from whom he received the money! And [the Gemara] answers: "Rather, [it is necessary in a case] where he took money from both of them, and it is not known, etc." And according to this, we say that even if he said that he knows, he should not be believed, because it was not incumbent upon him to pay close attention. Such is the approach of Rashi. And as for that which [Rashi] explained, that [the Gemara] asks on "if the item being purchased is not in his possession" (where it states that he is not deemed credible), and asks: "And let us see from whom he took the money?" — meaning, and to the one who gave him the money, he certainly consented [to sell] — this is difficult: For why should we believe him more than any ordinary single witness? For since the item being purchased is not in his possession, it is not applicable to apply a miggo in order to believe him! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained: "When the item being purchased is in his possession" — and then he is deemed credible on account of a miggo, as he could have said: "I did not sell [it]," or: "I repurchased it." But when "the item being purchased is not in his possession," he is not deemed credible, as then a miggo is not applicable. And [the Gemara] asks: "And let us see from whom he took the money" — granted that the item being purchased is in his possession, why is he deemed credible if he says concerning the one from whom he did not receive the money: "To this one I consented"? For [the baraita] implies that he is deemed credible in every case! And why should he be deemed credible? It would be a miggo in the face of witnesses (miggo bemakom eidim), for we are witnesses [i.e., it is self-evident] that he consented to the one who gave the money! And [the Gemara] answers: "Where he took money, etc." And according to this, we read the version: "And it is not known" [velo yedia], and we do not read the version: "And he did not know" [velo yada], which would imply that we do not care about his knowledge — for we certainly care about his knowledge if he knew! And according to this, we must say that he did not know, for if he knew, we would say he consented to this one. However, at the beginning of Bava Metzia (2b), regarding "Two who hold a garment," where the Gemara establishes it as a case of purchase and sale, and asks: "Purchase and sale? Let us see from whom he took the money!" — and Rashi explained there according to his approach here. And furthermore, he explained there: Even though it states in the last chapter of Kiddushin that when the item being purchased is not in his possession he is not deemed credible, and here it is considered as if the item is not in his possession, as both of them are holding the garment, so why does [the Gemara] ask that the seller should be deemed credible? Behold, we established there [in Kiddushin] that he took money from both of them, whereas now it entered [the Gemara's] mind that he took money from only one. However, according to Rabbeinu Tam's explanation, this is difficult: For what is the question there, "And let us see from whom he took the money?" Behold, according to his explanation, even if he took money from only one, we should not believe him, as I explained! Therefore, one must say there: "And let us see from whom he took the money" — that is to say, how can the Mishnah teach: "This one shall swear that he has no less than half of it, etc."? Let us ask the seller from whom he received the money, and let him be like a single witness, to exempt the one whom he supports even from an instituted oath (shevuat heiset), and to obligate his counterpart in a Torah oath! But to extract money from this one and give it to that one — it is obvious that he is not deemed credible, except as I explained. And [the Gemara] answers: "Where he took money from both of them." And according to this explanation as well, we read the version: "He did not know"; however, if he did know, it is obvious that we care about his knowledge, to obligate this one in a Torah oath, as I explained.
